messages:
inc-bot: PAGER: High error rate (5xx/timeouts) detected for model-runner-prod (svc=runtime). Alert threshold: 5xx > 2% over 2m. See: https://redwood.inc/alerts/AR-3321 :rotating_light:
Jules (oncall): I'm up. Pulling SLO dashboard now.
Jules (oncall): Confirming spikes across region-us-west-2, p50 latency up from 120ms -> 650ms, 5xx at 6.4% last 1m.
Ava Liao: Noted — any customer-facing incidents yet? CS dashboard showing a handful of user 5xx reports but not widespread.
Ravi Patel: I'm looking at runtime logs. I'm seeing repeated segfaults from model-runner pod group: `runtime_model_worker` with SIGSEGV in `kv_cache.c:274`.
Marta Gomez: Can you paste the stack/line?
Ravi Patel: Attaching recent tail:
```
# tail -n 80 /var/log/model-runner/runtime.log | grep -n "SIGSEGV" -A4
[2026-03-14T01:24:10Z] [worker-17] ERROR SIGSEGV at 0x7ffd1234
[2026-03-14T01:24:10Z] [worker-17] backtrace: 0x7f8a12ab kv_cache.c:274
[2026-03-14T01:24:10Z] [worker-17] last func: kv_cache_put
[2026-03-14T01:24:10Z] core dumped: /opt/redwood/bin/model-runner
```
Jules (oncall): That explains 5xx. Are pods OOMing or just segfaulting?
Theo - runtime: Looks like double-free in the kv cache when prefix caching and concurrent evictions hit. We pushed a safety check in staging last week; not present in prod binary.
Ava Liao: Are we able to mitigate without a full deploy? Options: - restart affected pods (rolling) - disable prefix caching via runtime flag - route traffic to the canary/compat model variant - add temporary circuit breaker to reduce concurrent requests per worker
Jules (oncall): I'm going to open a mitigation play. First step: scale down concurrency and enable circuit breaker in the routing layer to reduce pressure. Doing `curl -XPOST https://console.internal/route/model-runner-prod/actions -d '{"circuit_breaker": {"max_inflight": 8}}'`
deploy-bot: Route change accepted. New circuit breaker policy applied to 40% of nodes (gradual rollout).
Ravi Patel: After circuit breaker, 5xx dropped to ~3.1% in 30s but still above threshold. Latency p95 improved slightly.
Marta Gomez: While that stabilizes, can we identify if a particular model shard is triggering it?
Theo - runtime: Querying logs by model_id. `jq '.model_id' /var/log/model-runner/* | sort | uniq -c` shows model `rw-lm-13b-qc-v2` accounts for 72% of segfaults.
Ava Liao: That aligns with recent traffic shift from a customer who enabled long-context. Could be cache eviction pattern.
Jules (oncall): Next action: remove that model variant from prod routing and fallback to `rw-lm-13b-compat` for all new requests. I will create a route override.
deploy-bot: Route override created. 100% of new requests for `rw-lm-13b-qc-v2` will be routed to `rw-lm-13b-compat` for 10m.
Jules (oncall): Initiating rolling restart of model-runner pods in us-west-2 to clear corrupted state. Command: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/model-runner -n inference --grace-period=60`
Ravi Patel: Rolling restart started. Observing pods terminate and come back. No OOM kills reported in kube events.
Theo - runtime: I pulled a core from one of the crashed pods. Confirming crash at `kv_cache_put` when `evict_list` is NULL but still dereferenced. Patch ready: add null-check + backoff. I'll open hotfix PR.
Marta Gomez: Thanks. Any customer impact we should surface?
Ava Liao: CS: 18 customers reported transient 5xx in last 15m, 3 of which had production customers seeing degraded availability. None are on Dedicated instances; all hosted.
Jules (oncall): Creating incident page: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-03-model-runtime. Notifying SRE, runtime, and CS.
inc-bot: Incident page created and linked to pager.
Ravi Patel: Rolling restart completed. Post-restart metrics show 5xx at 0.6% and p95 latency back to baseline.
Ava Liao: I'm updating customers: short note drafted — "We've mitigated elevated error rates caused by a runtime cache bug; traffic has been stabilized and a hotfix is being deployed. We'll follow up with RCA and timeline." Any objections? :thumbsup:
Marta Gomez: :thumbsup:
Theo - runtime: Hotfix PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pulls/842. Patch adds safety checks and optional evict throttling. Requesting approval for hotfix patch to prod.
Jules (oncall): Can we do a canary deploy of the hotfix to 10% first?
deploy-bot: Canary deployment started for runtime-hotfix-842 to 10% in us-west-2.
Ravi Patel: Monitoring canary. No segfaults observed in canary for the last 5m.
Ava Liao: If canary looks good, schedule full rollout in 15m with 5m verification windows. I'll coordinate comms.
Jules (oncall): Handing incident to next on-call in 30m: @Ava Liao will be the primary follow-up for the postmortem and customer comms. I'll leave the incident open with status: mitigated, hotfix rolling.
Ava Liao: Taking handoff. Key actionables: 1) Full rollout of PR-842 if canary stays green. 2) Postmortem draft with root cause (double-free in kv_cache eviction), scope (customers affected), mitigation (circuit breaker + fallback routing + hotfix), and timeline. 3) Add integration test for concurrent eviction patterns.
Jules (oncall): Thanks team. Marking page severity P2 -> moved to monitoring. If anything regresses ping oncall.
inc-bot: Incident status updated: mitigated -> monitoring. Tags: runtime, segfault, hotfix-in-progress.
deploy-bot: Full rollout scheduled at 1863163500.
Theo - runtime: After full rollout, let's add runtime flag `--evict-backoff-ms` default 0 -> set to 50ms to reduce contention. I'll include in PR follow-up.
Ava Liao: Noted — will include that in postmortem action items.
Jules (oncall): Handoff done. Closing my on-call thread.
Ava Liao: Acknowledged — I'll keep the incident open until postmortem published.
